hypothesis: If the claim holds, the numeric ages of the Late Cretaceous (Chalk) stages on the chronostratigraphic chart will be at least about 300 million years before present.
pass_criterion: Age of the top of the Chalk-bearing Upper Cretaceous (base of Paleogene) and of the base of the Upper Cretaceous are both >= 300 Ma.
fail_criterion: Either age is < 300 Ma (for example, the Upper Cretaceous spans roughly 100.5-66 Ma). Failing this makes 'far more than 300 million years since the latter part of the Secondary' false.
interpretation: 'Secondary period' corresponds to the Mesozoic; 'latter part' corresponds to Late Cretaceous (Chalk). The test is on elapsed time since then, taken from radiometrically calibrated ages and not from Darwin's erosion-rate extrapolation. Modern reading: the erosion-rate assumption is not tested directly, only its implied elapsed time.

dataset.name: International Chronostratigraphic Chart
dataset.why_it_fits: The chart is downloadable and lists numeric boundary ages in Ma for the Cretaceous series and stages, so the Late Cretaceous start and end ages can be read directly.
